about: Spec 19 event catalog. Event parameters are from the USGS ComCat event pages linked in each entry (accessed 2026-09-24). Record-to-event links come from each PEER NGA-West2 file header (event name and date). The simulation's reference magnitude is a separate value (out/<record>/, data/richter readings.json) and is never replaced by these facts.

anza-2001.name: Anza-02 (Anza, California)
anza-2001.region: About 16 km ESE of Anza, California, USA
anza-2001.description: A moderate earthquake in southern California east-southeast of Anza. PEER's NGA-West2 database names this event Anza-02.

kocaeli-1999.name: Kocaeli (İzmit), Turkey
kocaeli-1999.region: About 4 km ESE of Derince, northwestern Turkey
kocaeli-1999.description: A large earthquake on the northern strand of the North Anatolian fault zone. USGS mapping associates it with a 145-km-long surface rupture.

sources.title: USGS: surface rupture and slip distribution of the 17 August 1999 İzmit earthquake

laquila-aftershock-2009.name: L'Aquila aftershock, Italy
laquila-aftershock-2009.region: Central Apennines, about 1 km SW of San Panfilo d'Ocre, Italy
laquila-aftershock-2009.description: The largest aftershock of the 6 April 2009 L'Aquila earthquake (Mw 6.3, USGS). These recordings are of this aftershock, not of the main shock.
laquila-aftershock-2009.reference_note: The simulation's reference magnitude for these records is 6.3, which matches the 6 April main shock rather than this Mw 5.5 aftershock. The simulation value is left unchanged.

sources.title: USGS event page usp000gvtu (6 April main shock)

niigata-2004.name: Niigata, Japan
niigata-2004.region: About 8 km SSW of Ojiya, Niigata Prefecture, Japan
niigata-2004.description: An earthquake in Niigata Prefecture, followed about 40 minutes later by an Mw 6.3 aftershock (USGS).

sources.title: PEER NGA-West2 ground motion database
sources.note: record source; header “Niigata Japan, 10/23/2004” (NGA-West2 labels aftershock records separately)

parkfield-2004.name: Parkfield, California
parkfield-2004.region: San Andreas Fault near Parkfield, central California, USA
parkfield-2004.description: A long-anticipated earthquake on the San Andreas Fault at Parkfield. The USGS describes it as the best-recorded earthquake to that date.

sources.title: USGS: introduction to the special issue on the 2004 Parkfield earthquake
